source.title: Understanding Generalization through Decision Pattern Shift
source.authors: Huiqi Deng; Yibo Li; Quanshi Zhang; Peng Zhang; Hong-Bin Pei; Xia Hu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is supplied
record.tranche_reason: Measures a different internal-decision-pattern property and its association with the generalization gap; it does not test the specific interventions or sharpness measure in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports decision-pattern shift (DPS) and its correlation with generalization gaps. It does not test memorization of random labels, width, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, optimizers, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Its OOD and shortcut-learning analyses are outside the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures GradCAM-based decision-pattern shift and its association with train–test loss gaps. None of V1–V8 names this measure. Label corruption is used to assess the diagnostic correlation, without reporting random-label fitting and held-out accuracy needed for V1. The study neither measures magnitude-aware weight sharpness nor compares its ranking with norm- or margin-based measures as required by V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the reported DPS–generalization-gap association and its weakening under label noise. The authors also interpret DPS spectra as organizing several generalization-failure regimes, while noting that semantically similar OOD data need not produce substantial shifts. Their interpretation of internal decision instability goes beyond establishing the reported correlations as causal mechanisms.
record.recipe_differences: Measures GradCAM-based channel-contribution decision patterns and their cosine shift; it does not reproduce the claim versions' interventions or magnitude-aware sharpness measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The DPS–gap correlation weakens as training-label noise increases: 0.930 at 0% noise, 0.855 at 20%, and a further decrease at 40%.

fits_no_version.finding: DPS correlates with per-sample loss gaps at r ≥ 0.78 across the studied architectures and datasets; class- and dataset-level associations are described qualitatively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GradCAM-based channel-contribution shifts from training class means are associated with train–test loss gaps in the studied image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: For VGG16 on CIFAR100, the DPS–loss-gap correlation declines from 0.930 with clean labels to 0.855 at 20% corruption and decreases further at 40%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The diagnostic association between DPS and loss gaps weakens when training-label corruption makes class-average reference patterns unreliable.

record.problems: The supplied text gives an aggregate sample-level correlation threshold rather than coefficients for each dataset and architecture; class- and dataset-level correlations are described without numerical coefficients. The 40% label-noise coefficient is not stated. The paper itself notes that its theoretical linearity is approximate and depends on assumptions about the relationship between aggregated pattern deviation and cosine-based DPS.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version results were reported in the supplied text. OOD, domain-shift, and shortcut-learning spectrum analyses are outside the specified versions and are not included as rows.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fixed-random-label fitting alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test-error changes when width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contributions of local connectivity or convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the penalty.
Dropout effects, small-data and excessive-dropout regimes, and removal of dropout with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples compared with equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The observed and partial states in the record describe DPS findings, not effects named by V1–V8. Accordingly, all rows remain linked to none and receive cannot_determine relative to these versions. No additional results bearing on a listed version appear in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Dropout effects and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
